blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: Every drain below the street sewer's flow line, like your floor drain, a basement bathroom, or a laundry line, normally relies on gravity to reach the sewer. An overhead sewer system reroutes those drains into a sump pit instead. An [ejector pump](/skokie/ejector-pump) lifts that wastewater up to a line above flood level, where a check valve keeps it from flowing back down. From there, gravity carries it the rest of the way to the street sewer, the same as every drain upstairs.

blocks.intro: In May 2020, Skokie got 7.35 inches of rain in five days. The Village encouraged homeowners with basement backups to consider a backflow valve or an overhead sewer.

items.body: The floor drain, laundry tub and basement toilet all sit below the street sewer.
Most conversions here route the laundry and floor drain into the new pit.
A partly blocked lateral can cause backups too. A [sewer repair](/skokie/sewer-repair) may be all you need.

blocks.h2: Overhead Sewer Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: How does an overhead sewer keep my basement dry?
items.preview: Basement drains no longer connect to the sewer by gravity.
items.answer: Basement drains empty into a sealed pit, and a pump lifts the water to a pipe near the ceiling. It leaves the house above the level where the sewer can back up.

items.q: Can the laundry tub stay in the basement?
items.answer: Yes. It drains into the new pit along with the floor drain.
No. An overhead sewer handles sewer backups. Groundwater needs a [sump pump](/skokie/sump-pumps).

items.q: How long does a conversion take?
items.answer: Usually a few days, depending on the layout and the number of fixtures.

items.q: How much does an overhead sewer cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on your basement. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the sewer depth, the layout, the fixtures and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
